name: Digoxin
executiveSummary: Cardiac glycoside. Adult maintenance: **0.125–0.25 mg PO/day** (elderly/CKD **0.0625–0.125 mg**). Load (if needed): **0.25–0.5 mg** IV/PO divided. Usual HF target level **0.5–0.9 ng/mL**. Toxicity ↑ with hypokalemia.
indications:
## Indications

- HFrEF (symptoms despite optimal therapy); rate control in AF (2nd line vs beta-blockers/CCBs).

## Precautions

- Narrow therapeutic index — levels, ECG, K+/Mg2+/renal function.
- Interactions: amiodarone, verapamil, macrolides ↑ digoxin level.
- Antidote: digoxin-specific Fab in severe poisoning.

> Not a modern acute rescue inotrope (prefer other shock strategies).

adulto.dose: Maintenance: **0.125–0.25 mg PO/day**. CKD/elderly: **0.0625–0.125 mg/day**. Total load guide **0.5–1 mg** in 24 h divided (slow IV or PO) — many start without load.
adulto.administration: PO. Slow IV ≥5 min diluted; not IM.

pediatrico.dose: Total load often **20–40 µg/kg** (preterms less) divided; maintenance **5–10 µg/kg/day** — pediatric cardiology.

stability:
## Stability

- Ampoule: use after opening per label.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Nausea, anorexia, blurred/xanthopsia vision, arrhythmias (bigeminy, VT), confusion — suspect toxicity.
